articles.title: In Likely a Culver City Record, Black Equities Buys Multifamily Asset for $106M
articles.narrative: Black Equities has acquired Access Culver City, a 115-unit mixed-use property with 31,000 square feet of ground-floor retail, for $106 million. The transaction, which involved seller Greystar, is believed to be the largest multifamily deal in Culver City's history. The acquisition highlights Culver City's strong appeal as a multifamily investment market, driven by its concentration of media and technology employers and supportive housing policies.

data_points.notable_features: Includes 31,000 square feet of fully leased ground-floor retail.
data_points.project_notes: The property is approximately a decade old. The purchase price was allocated as $81 million for the residential component and $25 million for the retail space.

articles.market_intelligence: Culver City is one of Southern California's hottest multifamily investment markets, driven by media and technology employers and pro-development housing policies. The city has more than 4,500 housing units in the pipeline and is attracting significant multifamily investment within Los Angeles County.

articles.title: Palm Beach County Pauses Data Center Applications
articles.narrative: The Palm Beach County Commission has implemented a temporary moratorium on new data center applications in unincorporated areas, citing concerns from residents regarding infrastructure, resource consumption, and long-term impacts. This pause, enacted through a 5-2 vote, allows the county to develop appropriate zoning regulations for this asset class. The moratorium is expected to last up to a year or until new zoning is adopted, though one large-scale project, Central Park Commerce Center, will proceed with its review as it was filed prior to the suspension.

data_points.notable_features: Located near the Arden residential development and Saddle View Elementary School, facing Route 98.
data_points.project_notes: Also known as Project Tango, this development was filed before the moratorium and will be allowed to undergo review.

articles.title: Douglaston Realty Offloads 7 Cornelia Street in West Village for $25M
articles.narrative: A shell corporation, with financing arranged by an investor linked to SoJo Spa Club owner Eun Rae Jo, has acquired 7 Cornelia Street in the West Village for $25 million. Douglaston Realty Management and its partners sold the five-story prewar building, which features 47 apartments and two ground-floor retail spaces. The transaction was financed with a $17.6 million mortgage from Woori America Bank.

articles.title: Siemens Financial, First Horizon Lend $65M on Palm Beach Gardens Medical Complex

The development will feature a two-story neighborhood hospital and a three-story medical outpatient building, fully pre-leased to Jupiter Medical Center. This project aims to expand access to high-quality healthcare within the Avenir master-planned community.

articles.title: Twain Capital Supplies $65M C-PACE Loan for Colorado Hotel Project
articles.narrative: Twain Capital Partners has provided a $65 million C-PACE loan to Nathaniel Kelly Foote for the Foote's Rest mixed-use development in Frisco, CO. The project, anchored by an 80-key Marriott Tribute Hotel, will also feature an entertainment venue, ballroom, event space, conference center, restaurants, and a rooftop bar. The financing leverages Colorado's robust C-PACE program, which allows property owners to fund 100 percent of sustainability upgrades, and addresses the strong hospitality demand and limited hotel supply in the Frisco market.

data_points.notable_features: Mixed-use development anchored by a Marriott Tribute Hotel, featuring an underground 13,500 SF entertainment venue with bowling lanes and golf swing suites, a 4,000 SF ballroom, 1,500 SF of event space, a conference center, restaurants, and a 10,000 SF rooftop bar.
data_points.project_notes: C-PACE loan for a mixed-use project.

articles.market_intelligence: The C-PACE market has seen significant growth, with average transaction sizes increasing from $5 million-$10 million to over $25 million, and several $100 million-plus C-PACE financings closing in the last 12 months, indicating its increasing role in capital stacks.

articles.title: Raven Capital Completes 33-Story Multifamily High-Rise in Houston’s Museum District

The property features 475 units, including 55 boutique hotel suites, and offers a range of amenities such as a pool, fitness and recovery areas, and coworking space. The building also includes a cocktail lounge and raw bar on its 12th floor.

This phase will deliver 273 units designated for households earning 70 percent or less of the area median income, along with a one-acre public park. Redstone Bank provided the construction loan, complemented by federal and state tax credit equity and other subsidies, with completion anticipated in 2029.

The project, designed by Cedar Corporation, adds new office space, shop space, and a wash bay to the county's existing maintenance campus, enhancing highway operations and service capacity for the eastern portion of St. Croix County.

The transaction includes a Tru by Hilton and a Home2 Suites by Hilton, marking the firm's second and third hotel sales in recent years and highlighting its growth in the hospitality sector.

articles.title: Housing Notes: The housing usually wins
articles.narrative: This opinion piece argues that the increasing financialization of housing through prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket is problematic, turning shelter into a speculative asset rather than a fundamental need. The author draws parallels to the inherent issues of gambling, noting how these platforms can amplify market sentiment beyond fundamentals and encourage retail speculation, reminiscent of the lead-up to the Great Financial Crisis. The author also criticizes news outlets like CNBC and CNN for promoting these platforms without consistent disclosure of their financial relationships, suggesting a potential conflict of interest that misleads viewers about the reliability of these prediction markets.

articles.title: NY Dirt: Hit the gym
articles.narrative: The New York City retail market is experiencing a significant surge in high-end wellness concepts, with boutique gyms and health-focused medical groups driving leasing activity. This trend is highlighted by major leases such as Chelsea Piers' 76,000-square-foot deal at 250 Water Street and Life Time's 71,000-square-foot lease in North Williamsburg. The increased demand for self-care and mental well-being, a lasting impact of the Covid-19 pandemic, has contributed to record-low retail vacancies in Manhattan's prime submarkets, with Madison Avenue and Soho reporting the lowest availability rates.
articles.market_intelligence: Retail vacancies in Manhattan's prime submarkets reached a record low of approximately 12% in the past quarter, the lowest since JLL began reporting in late 2019. Madison Avenue on the Upper East Side and Soho recorded the lowest availability rates at 8%.

articles.title: Related Ross appointment fires up West Palm Beach development debate
articles.narrative: West Palm Beach residents are expressing significant opposition to the city commission's appointment of a Related Ross executive to the Downtown Development Authority, intensifying an ongoing debate about rapid development in the city. Critics, including the "Save West Palm Beach" group, argue that the city is prioritizing developer interests over community input and moving too quickly with high-rise construction, aiming to transform the area into a financial hub. The appointment of a second Related Ross executive to the DDA has fueled accusations of favoritism towards developers. In response to the backlash, Mayor Keith James announced a pause on the downtown master plan and the formation of a resident-led coalition to increase community involvement in future development decisions.

The 25-story development, which includes ground-floor retail and an 11-story parking garage with a rooftop amenity deck, has begun the permitting process. This revival follows a period of legal challenges for Cohen, including other debt-related lawsuits in New York, and comes as downtown West Palm Beach has seen significant office market growth.

articles.title: Could Chicago’s office buildings benefit from the AI boom? Research says yes
articles.narrative: The artificial intelligence boom, which has significantly boosted office space demand in New York City and San Francisco, is expected to create spillover benefits for other major markets, including Chicago. According to VTS data cited by Bloomberg, building tours by AI companies have surged 85 percent this year, with a growing number of these companies also exploring options in Seattle and Chicago. This trend could offer much-needed vacancy relief for Chicago's office market, particularly as competition for premium space intensifies in established tech hubs.

articles.title: This time, San Francisco’s office boom is flowing south
articles.narrative: The Bay Area office market is experiencing a unique boom driven by artificial intelligence companies, with San Francisco-based firms increasingly expanding southward into Silicon Valley for spacious office campuses. This trend has significantly reduced Silicon Valley's office vacancy rate and inspired major tenants to renew large leases. Despite high overall vacancy in San Francisco, the demand for premium 'trophy' office spaces remains strong, with some experts anticipating new construction in the city's residential-adjacent neighborhoods. The East Bay, particularly Oakland, has lagged in recovery but is expected to see a shift as the market continues to evolve.
articles.market_intelligence: San Francisco's office leasing boom is accelerating, with a notable inversion where AI companies originating in San Francisco are expanding into Silicon Valley. Silicon Valley's office vacancy rate has fallen to 14.1% from 16% last year, and Sunnyvale's vacancy rate dropped from 15.2% to 9.8% year-over-year. Subleasable office space in Silicon Valley is at its lowest since 2016, with 1.3 million square feet available. In San Francisco, rents for premium spaces have increased 40% year-over-year to $140 per square foot, while the citywide average asking rent is $66 per square foot. Class B vacancy in San Francisco fell from 33.4% to 30% year-over-year, and Class C fell from 20.3% to 15.8%. Downtown Oakland's total vacancy increased from 30.3% to 32.3% year-over-year, with Emeryville having the highest average asking rent in the East Bay at $4.28.

articles.title: “Diego & I”: SF apartment building formerly occupied by Frida Kahlo, Diego Rivera hits market
articles.narrative: An 11-unit apartment building on Telegraph Hill in San Francisco, notable for its historical connection to artists Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera, has been listed for sale for $8 million. The Art Moderne property, built into a cliffside in 1938, is fully leased and represents a unique development that would be challenging to replicate under current seismic and permitting regulations. The building's full occupancy reflects San Francisco's tight housing market.

data_points.notable_features: Art Moderne building constructed into a sheer cliff; formerly occupied by Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera; featured as a filming location for the 1952 film "The Sniper".
data_points.project_notes: Site was created from an illegal quarry blast in the early 1900s. Units are up to 950 square feet, with lower units requiring multiple flights of stairs to street level.

articles.market_intelligence: San Francisco's housing market is rapidly tightening due to growing demand and shrinking supply.

articles.title: SF approves another condo project for fast-densifying Market Street corner
articles.narrative: San Francisco officials have granted final approval for a 23-story, 201-unit condominium tower at 1965 Market Street, a site that has been entitled for development for over a decade. The project, owned by Keller Grover, incorporates a historic Mission Revival building and includes 28 affordable units. Brokers anticipate the newly approved site will be listed for sale and could set a new precedent for development land values under California's updated housing laws, particularly Senate Bill 423, which streamlines housing approvals.

data_points.notable_features: The project incorporates a historic Mission Revival building, repurposing it for the condo building's lobby and amenities entrance.
data_points.project_notes: The project evolved from a 7-story, 96-unit proposal in 2015 to a 23-story tower by leveraging state density bonus measures and Senate Bill 423. It includes 28 affordable units for households earning less than 50% of the area's median income.

articles.title: There are no offices being built in Philadelphia
articles.narrative: Philadelphia's office development pipeline has stalled, with no new projects underway following the completion of a 438,000-square-foot build-to-suit for an insurance company. This lack of new construction is largely attributed to a scarcity of anchor tenants willing to commit to space years in advance. While the central business district saw a drop in vacancy to 19.8% and positive absorption in Q2, this was primarily driven by the insurance company's move. Overall office inventory and sublease space are decreasing, partly due to conversions, though suburban office leasing activity has also significantly slowed.

articles.title: 'Not Happy, But Comfortable': CREFC President On CRE Finding A New Normal
articles.narrative: A recent survey by the CRE Finance Council (CREFC) indicates a cautiously optimistic sentiment within the commercial real estate industry, with a slight uptick in market sentiment compared to the previous quarter. While only a small percentage of respondents expressed negative views for 2027, the majority remained neutral, suggesting a period of stabilization rather than strong recovery. CREFC President and CEO Lisa Pendergast noted that despite the current challenges, the industry is adapting to elevated interest rates, finding a new equilibrium where it can manage within the existing financial landscape, even if not entirely content with it. She believes the industry's resilience, honed through past crises like the pandemic and the Global Financial Crisis, is enabling it to navigate the current environment.

articles.title: Data Center Pipeline Slows As Canceled Projects Pile Up
articles.narrative: The pipeline for new data center projects is showing signs of moderation, despite continued high demand for AI capacity and record overall U.S. construction levels. While data center construction spending reached a new high of $50 billion in April, the number of planned projects dipped in June, contributing to an overall decline in commercial project planning. This slowdown is attributed to increased local opposition and regulatory hurdles, with several large-scale projects recently canceled or rejected in Virginia and North Carolina, and numerous jurisdictions across 14 states considering bans on new digital infrastructure developments.

articles.title: Mavik Capital Looks To Raise $1B, Targeting Distressed Real Estate
articles.narrative: Mavik Capital Management, a New York-based investment firm, is actively seeking to raise $1 billion for its new distressed real estate fund, VS3. The fund will target a variety of distressed commercial real estate assets, including hard assets and commercial mortgage-backed securities, capitalizing on market dislocations and the significant need for capital, restructurings, and recapitalizations. This initiative follows the success of two prior funds, VS1 and VS2, which collectively raised over $1 billion, demonstrating Mavik's established presence in the distressed asset space and its ability to act as an alternative lender amid a pullback from traditional regional players.

data_points.project_notes: Mavik Capital Management is raising capital for its new distress fund, VS3, targeting $1 billion. The firm previously raised $335 million for VS1 and $685 million for VS2, which closed in 2025.

articles.market_intelligence: Many investors are seeking distressed commercial real estate deals due to post-pandemic shifts in the office sector and financial stress from elevated interest rates. Starwood Capital Group recently closed a $10.2 billion opportunistic real estate fund, Starwood Distressed Opportunity Fund XIII, which has already committed $3 billion of equity to 20 transactions.

articles.title: Denver's Population Slowdown Is A Hurdle For Otherwise Stable Industrial Market
articles.narrative: Denver's industrial market, while stable with an 8.6% vacancy rate, faces a significant hurdle due to slowing population growth, which experts believe is essential for the city to become a top-tier industrial hub. The region's population growth has decelerated, with a 2.5% increase from 2020 to 2024 compared to 6.4% in the prior four-year period, largely attributed to Denver's high cost of living and labor. This slowdown is causing some tenants to seek cheaper operating environments in other markets like Reno, Las Vegas, or Salt Lake City. Despite these challenges, Denver remains an appealing market for investors, with capital partners applying 6% cap rates, though it is perceived to be at a tipping point compared to more rapidly growing industrial markets like Phoenix and Salt Lake City.
articles.market_intelligence: Denver's industrial market vacancy rate has been stable at around 8.6% for the last three quarters. Net absorption in Denver declined 83% quarter-over-quarter, with the last quarter of negative net absorption occurring in Q1 2010. The Denver-Aurora-Centennial metro area's population increased by 2.5% from 2020 to 2024, a decrease from the 6.4% increase seen from 2016 to 2020. Colorado's annual population growth rate in 2025 was 0.4%, the lowest since 1989. In contrast, the Phoenix metro saw net absorption down 7.7% quarter-over-quarter but up 7.5% year-over-year. The Phoenix-Mesa-Chandler metro's population increased nearly 3.5% from 2020 to 2024 and 1.1% from 2024 to 2025. Investment sales in Denver are seeing capital partners apply 6% cap rates.
